active_paradigms.idea: Replace the many correlated SLSQP restarts with one constrained differential-evolution search over a topology-reduced asymmetric packing family
active_paradigms.description: The current constructor is a multistart SLSQP formulation in all 78 center/radius variables. Its strengths are exact analytic constraint Jacobians, several grid/hex starts, and a final feasibility shrink; its main weakness is that SLSQP is local and uniform shrinking can erase the small gain from an otherwise excellent unequal-radius solution. Define a lower-dimensional explicit family based on six staggered rows with variable row heights, horizontal offsets, and independently perturbed boundary/interior circle radii, while retaining a few unrestricted defect circles near the locations where a 5-by-5 grid has excess space. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on these family parameters, with a scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint representing walls and all pair distances, and objective negative total radius. Seed its initial population with the current grid and centered-hex arrangements, but also include reflected and deliberately asymmetric defect placements. Use `updating='deferred'`, `workers=1`, a fixed seed, moderate `popsize` around 6 to 10, and a strict finite maximum iteration budget that fits the timeout. The reduced parameterization is crucial: differential evolution over the raw 78 coordinates is unlikely to converge in time, whereas it can choose between distinct row/contact topologies that SLSQP cannot escape. Return the best directly feasible population member, with only a tiny safety contraction of radii rather than the current potentially large uniform repair.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current local contact graph and improve the actual validated sum of radii above roughly 2.62893; reported_sum is not an objective because the evaluator recomputes `np.sum(radii)`.
active_paradigms.cautions: The evaluator permits only about 1e-6 of wall or overlap tolerance, so constraint values must be based on unsquared distances or carefully scaled squared distances and the final contraction should be on the order of 1e-8, not 1e-4. Do not use an unconstrained penalty whose infeasible candidates can dominate. Keep dimensionality low and evaluate pair constraints vectorially, otherwise population evaluations may consume the 350-second subprocess budget.

active_paradigms.idea: Hard-code a discovered maximal contact graph and solve its tangency/KKT equations with nonlinear least squares
active_paradigms.description: Near an optimum, almost every useful circle is pinned by wall contacts and tangencies, so continuing to optimize through all 325 inactive pair inequalities is poorly conditioned. First inspect the best known packing offline and identify the active wall contacts and circle-circle contact graph, including asymmetric defects rather than forcing a globally symmetric hex lattice. Encode an explicit candidate with variables for all centers, radii, and nonnegative contact multipliers. In a single scipy.optimize.least_squares call, solve residuals consisting of active tangency equations `||ci-cj||-(ri+rj)=0`, active wall equations, and the KKT stationarity equations for the sum-of-radii objective; use multiplier variables in log or squared form to enforce nonnegativity. Add very small residual weights for a selected set of inactive-pair clearance targets only when needed to eliminate mechanisms, while retaining a full post-call vectorized feasibility test. This is a fundamentally different use of geometry from the current generic SLSQP: it searches the algebraic manifold of one hypothesized jammed packing and can converge to much tighter contacts than numerical inequality optimization. Try several candidate graphs as separately hard-coded constructors across program revisions, not by solving a graph-selection problem during evaluation. A successful graph produces a reproducible explicit numerical constructor with minimal runtime and no dependence on random local-search outcomes.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Recover the final 0.006 or more that can be lost to SLSQP termination, repair shrinkage, and an incorrect local active set, while preserving strict feasibility.
active_paradigms.cautions: Least-squares residual zero alone does not prove global non-overlap: validate every one of the 325 pairs and all walls afterward, then apply a tiny radius-only safety factor if necessary. A tangency graph can be underconstrained or have a mirror/mechanism; KKT stationarity and enough wall contacts are needed to remove these null modes. This method depends on accurately extracting a viable contact graph from an existing high-quality result, and should not be used as an unstructured 78-variable least-squares fit without the stationarity/contact structure.

active_paradigms.idea: For every explicit center pattern, compute globally optimal radii by one linear program instead of sequential pairwise radius scaling
active_paradigms.description: For fixed centers, maximizing the radius sum is exactly a linear program: set each radius upper bound to its minimum distance to a wall, and impose `ri + rj <= ||ci-cj||` for every pair. The current `compute_max_radii` performs an order-dependent proportional reduction, and the main `repair` performs an even more conservative global scaling; neither is the optimum radius assignment for fixed centers. Replace either repair path for a chosen explicit asymmetric center constructor by a single scipy.optimize.linprog call with objective `-ones(26)`, pairwise inequality matrix rows containing ones in columns i and j, and bounds `(0, wall_limit_i)`. Use the resulting radii directly, then contract by approximately 1e-8 to protect against floating point distance error. This permits center designs with intentionally close pairs: the LP allocates the available separation to the circles where radius is most valuable rather than shrinking all circles proportionally. Design the centers from a staggered hex core plus boundary and diagonal defects, and evaluate a small fixed list of such explicit arrays; each array needs only one LP call, not an optimizer pipeline. Since the LP has only 26 variables and 325 inequalities, HiGHS solves essentially instantly and makes scores deterministic.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase validated sum of radii for explicit geometric center layouts by obtaining the true best unequal radii at those centers, eliminating avoidable loss from conservative/order-dependent repair.
active_paradigms.cautions: This optimizes radii only; it cannot by itself move centers beyond the quality of the explicit pattern. Pair distances must be computed from the final returned centers, and zero/near-zero duplicate centers should be excluded because they force zero radii. The evaluator requires exactly arrays of shapes `(26,2)` and `(26,)`; do not return LP status objects, and compute reported_sum from the final safety-contracted radii.
